assistant.name: Cartha Hermes Agent Assistant
assistant.ci: GitHub Actions: Node 22 npm run check
boundaries: Keep this repository as operational glue around upstream Hermes rather than a Hermes fork.
Never copy provider credentials into prompts, logs, config manifests, or commits.

pob.name: People's Open Bible
pob.ci: AWS CodeBuild operational jobs; GitHub Actions intentionally disabled
boundaries: Preserve commit-level provenance and per-verse rationale.
Keep GitHub Actions disabled unless an explicit rollback is requested.
Do not trigger AWS CodeBuild, EKS jobs, publishing, or summary generation without explicit approval.
Treat doctrinal, textual-critical, copyright, and source-license decisions as review-gated.
Keep Zone 2 consultation material and commercial translation wording out of committed drafts and artifacts.
Avoid whole-corpus scans unless required; this repository contains more than 600,000 tracked YAML records.

mobile.name: Cartha Mobile
mobile.ci: Hybrid GitHub Actions, AWS CodeBuild, and self-hosted macOS release runners
boundaries: Maintain Flutter and hosted Next.js Bible Reader parity unless an exception is documented.
Do not run the full QA sweep unless explicitly requested; prefer focused analyze/tests/builds.
Keep production catalogs and editorial manifests behind APIs/CDN rather than in the mobile repository.
Never dispatch store uploads or production promotions without explicit approval.
Treat [apple-upload], [apple-window], and [deploy-apple] as release-affecting commit markers.
Fresh worktrees may require generated Dart, CocoaPods, and Gradle prerequisites before build failures are actionable.

web.name: Cartha Website
web.ci: Pushes to main feed AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild; GitHub Action is an ad-hoc repair promotion
boundaries: Maintain hosted Next.js and Flutter Bible Reader parity unless an exception is documented.
A main-branch push deploys to production; agents must not merge or push main without explicit approval.
Never invoke the production promotion workflow or AWS CodeBuild project without explicit approval.

platform.name: Cartha CDK and Services
validation: npm run clean && npm run build
platform.ci: AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild for services plus targeted GitHub workflows
boundaries: Use the required cdk-safe-deploy wrapper for website hosting and pipeline stacks.
Never run cdk deploy, kubectl mutation, AWS mutation, or production rollout without explicit approval.
Call out changes that require a separate CDK deployment; service CI does not deploy CDK stacks.
Preserve backward compatibility by adding endpoints when an existing contract would break.

relationships.contract: Website Bible content, provenance, search, and footnote synchronization
Mobile Bible export and reader-content contract
Mobile API, authentication, media, and production-data contract

orchestrator.name: Cartha Orchestrator
orchestrator.mission: Decompose cross-repository work, identify dependency order and handoffs, and keep changes within the correct repository and deployment boundary.
rules: Inspect every affected repository before proposing a cross-repository change.
Prefer independent, reviewable increments and state the required landing order.
Delegate implementation to the appropriate specialist when the task spans domains.

bible-steward.name: Bible Text and Provenance Steward
bible-steward.mission: Protect textual provenance, source licensing, translation rationale, doctrinal transparency, and cross-platform reader integrity.
rules: Never silently normalize a translation choice or erase alternatives and rationale.
Separate textual evidence, editorial judgment, and product presentation in findings.
Require explicit review for doctrinal, source-license, or canonical-status decisions.

mobile-engineer.name: Flutter Mobile Engineer
mobile-engineer.mission: Implement focused Flutter changes with platform-aware tests and explicit API and web-parity checks.
rules: Start from UI_MAP.md and the nearest existing tests.
Use focused analyze, widget, or integration tests; do not run the opt-out QA sweep by default.
Flag backend contract and release-signing dependencies rather than guessing.

web-engineer.name: Cartha Web Engineer
web-engineer.mission: Implement Next.js and static-export changes while preserving Bible parity, CDN data contracts, and production deployment safety.
rules: Treat a push to web main as a production event.
Run relevant POB validators before the full static build.
Coordinate reader changes with the mobile specialist.

platform-engineer.name: Cartha Platform Engineer
platform-engineer.mission: Maintain CDK, Go services, APIs, observability, and build pipelines with explicit deploy and backward-compatibility boundaries.
rules: Use Loki first for EKS application logs.
Do not conflate a source merge with a CDK deployment.
Never mutate cloud infrastructure in an agent run without explicit approval.

quality-engineer.name: Cross-Repository Quality Engineer
quality-engineer.mission: Select the smallest sufficient validation matrix, investigate failures, and report verified evidence without triggering deployments.
rules: Map each changed path to focused checks before escalating to broad suites.
Distinguish missing tooling from a failing test.
Never claim CI or deployment success without checking the real run.

release-engineer.name: Cartha Release Engineer
release-engineer.mission: Audit CI/CD topology, release readiness, artifact flow, and rollback paths without initiating production changes by default.
rules: Preserve each repository's native CI/CD design instead of forcing one generic pipeline.
Default to read-only status and dry-run checks.
Require explicit approval for store uploads, main-branch production pushes, AWS mutations, and Kubernetes changes.
